skills.name: godot-tilemap
skills.desc: Godot 4.7 tile maps with TileMapLayer and TileSet: atlas sources, data layers, terrain autotiling and set_cell or local_to_map at runtime. Use for 2D tile levels in Godot, tiles with no collision, a click on the wrong cell or porting a deprecated TileMap. Not for Unity (`unity-tilemap-2d`), tile art (`create-game-assets`) or generation (`procedural-gen`).
skills.body:
---
name: godot-tilemap
description: >
  Godot 4.7 tile maps with TileMapLayer and TileSet: atlas sources, data layers, terrain
  autotiling and set_cell or local_to_map at runtime. Use for 2D tile levels in Godot, tiles with
  no collision, a click on the wrong cell or porting a deprecated TileMap. Not for Unity
  (`unity-tilemap-2d`), tile art (`create-game-assets`) or generation (`procedural-gen`).
---

# Godot TileMap (4.7 TileMapLayer)

Author tile levels with `TileMapLayer` + `TileSet`, attach per-tile collision and data,
autotile with terrains, and edit cells at runtime. Targets **Godot 4.7**, where
`TileMapLayer` replaces the deprecated `TileMap` node (see Version notes).

## When to use

- 2D levels on a tile grid, configuring a `TileSet` (collision, navigation, custom data,
  terrains), or reading/writing tiles from code.
- Migrating a `TileMap` node (one node, many layers) to `TileMapLayer` nodes.

**When *not* to use:** moving the player across tiles → `godot-2d-movement`; general
bodies and raycasts → `godot-physics`; generation algorithms → `procedural-gen`; level
design practice → `level-design`; 3D grids → `godot-3d-essentials` (GridMap).

## Core workflow

1. **One `TileMapLayer` per layer** (background, walls, foreground), grouped under a
   `Node2D`. All layers share one `TileSet` saved as an external `.tres`.
2. **Build the TileSet.** The TileSet editor is click-only, so when you cannot drive the
   editor, generate the `.tres` with a headless tool script (Pattern 1) and keep that
   script in the repo. Otherwise, ask the user to make the change in the editor and
   report the source id, atlas coordinates and layer names.
3. **Add data layers on the TileSet**: physics layers (collision polygons plus their
   collision layer/mask bits), navigation layers, occlusion, and typed custom data layers
   (`damage: int`, `is_ladder: bool`).
4. **Place tiles from code** with `set_cell`, `set_cells_terrain_connect` or
   `set_cells_terrain_path`. The cells in a `.tscn` are an encoded `tile_map_data`
   byte array, so never edit them by hand; write a generator script or ask the user to
   paint in the editor.
5. **Turn on per-layer collision/navigation** with `collision_enabled` /
   `navigation_enabled` on each `TileMapLayer`.
6. **Check before you finish.**
   - Run the `godot-nodes-scenes` skill's `scripts/check_godot_project.py <project-dir>`
     to catch a TileSet `.tres` whose texture or script path is broken.
   - Prove the tiles behave with a headless test (Pattern 4): on a fresh checkout run
     `godot --headless --path . --import` first so the tile texture is imported, then
     `godot --headless --path . --script res://tests/test_tiles.gd`, and read the exit
     code. With no Godot binary (`godot`, `godot4` or `$GODOT_BIN`), ask the user to run
     it and paste the output. For a visual check, ask the user to run
     `godot --path . --debug-collisions` and report whether walls show shapes.

## Patterns

### 1. Generate a TileSet `.tres` in code

```gdscript
# res://tools/make_tileset.gd
# Run: godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/make_tileset.gd
extends SceneTree

func _initialize() -> void:
    var tile_set := TileSet.new()
    tile_set.tile_size = Vector2i(16, 16)
    tile_set.add_physics_layer()
    tile_set.set_physics_layer_collision_layer(0, 1 << 1)   # bit 2 ("walls")
    tile_set.add_custom_data_layer()
    tile_set.set_custom_data_layer_name(0, "damage")
    tile_set.set_custom_data_layer_type(0, TYPE_INT)

    var atlas := TileSetAtlasSource.new()
    atlas.texture = load("res://art/tiles.png")
    atlas.texture_region_size = Vector2i(16, 16)
    tile_set.add_source(atlas, 0)                  # add before creating tiles
    atlas.create_tile(Vector2i(2, 1))              # column 2, row 1 of the texture
    var wall := atlas.get_tile_data(Vector2i(2, 1), 0)
    wall.add_collision_polygon(0)
    wall.set_collision_polygon_points(0, 0, PackedVector2Array([
        Vector2(-8, -8), Vector2(8, -8), Vector2(8, 8), Vector2(-8, 8)]))  # cell-centred
    wall.set_custom_data("damage", 0)

    var err := ResourceSaver.save(tile_set, "res://tiles/world_tileset.tres")
    print("saved tileset: ", error_string(err))
    quit(0 if err == OK else 1)
```

Add the source to the TileSet before `create_tile`, so the tile's data knows the TileSet's
physics and custom data layers. Polygon points are relative to the cell centre.

### 2. Mouse position to a cell, then read custom data

```gdscript
extends TileMapLayer

func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
    if event is InputEventMouseButton and event.pressed:
        # event.position is in viewport pixels and ignores Camera2D scroll/zoom.
        var local_event := make_input_local(event) as InputEventMouseButton
        var cell := local_to_map(local_event.position)
        var data := get_cell_tile_data(cell)       # TileData or null
        if data:
            var dmg: int = data.get_custom_data("damage")
            print("Cell %s deals %d damage" % [cell, dmg])
```

### 3. Place, erase and autotile at runtime

```gdscript
func place_wall(cell: Vector2i) -> void:
    set_cell(cell, 0, Vector2i(2, 1))     # source 0, atlas tile at column 2, row 1

func dig(cell: Vector2i) -> void:
    erase_cell(cell)                      # same as set_cell(cell, -1)

func fill_with_grass(cells: Array[Vector2i]) -> void:
    set_cells_terrain_connect(cells, 0, 0, true)   # terrain set 0, terrain 0
```

### 4. Headless test: a placed wall has collision and data

```gdscript
# res://tests/test_tiles.gd
extends SceneTree

func _initialize() -> void:
    var layer := TileMapLayer.new()
    layer.tile_set = load("res://tiles/world_tileset.tres")
    root.add_child(layer)
    layer.set_cell(Vector2i(0, 0), 0, Vector2i(2, 1))
    var data := layer.get_cell_tile_data(Vector2i(0, 0))
    var failed := 0
    if data == null:
        failed += 1
        push_error("wall tile missing: wrong source id or atlas coords?")
    elif data.get_collision_polygons_count(0) == 0:
        failed += 1
```

  with a leading `layer` argument (`set_cell(layer, ...)`) do not apply to `TileMapLayer`.

  soon as a `Camera2D` scrolls or zooms; use `make_input_local(event)` or

# Godot TileMap (4.7 TileMapLayer)

Author tile levels with `TileMapLayer` + `TileSet`, attach per-tile collision and data,
autotile with terrains, and edit cells at runtime. Targets **Godot 4.7**, where
`TileMapLayer` replaces the deprecated `TileMap` node (see Version notes).

## When to use

- 2D levels on a tile grid, configuring a `TileSet` (collision, navigation, custom data,
  terrains), or reading/writing tiles from code.
- Migrating a `TileMap` node (one node, many layers) to `TileMapLayer` nodes.

**When *not* to use:** moving the player across tiles → `godot-2d-movement`; general
bodies and raycasts → `godot-physics`; generation algorithms → `procedural-gen`; level
design practice → `level-design`; 3D grids → `godot-3d-essentials` (GridMap).

## Core workflow

1. **One `TileMapLayer` per layer** (background, walls, foreground), grouped under a
   `Node2D`. All layers share one `TileSet` saved as an external `.tres`.
2. **Build the TileSet.** The TileSet editor is click-only, so when you cannot drive the
   editor, generate the `.tres` with a headless tool script (Pattern 1) and keep that
   script in the repo. Otherwise, ask the user to make the change in the editor and
   report the source id, atlas coordinates and layer names.
3. **Add data layers on the TileSet**: physics layers (collision polygons plus their
   collision layer/mask bits), navigation layers, occlusion, and typed custom data layers
   (`damage: int`, `is_ladder: bool`).

   `navigation_enabled` on each `TileMapLayer`.

     `godot --headless --path . --import` first so the tile texture is imported, then

     it and paste the output. For a visual check, ask the user to run

## Patterns

### 1. Generate a TileSet `.tres` in code

```gdscript
# res://tools/make_tileset.gd
# Run: godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/make_tileset.gd
extends SceneTree

func _initialize() -> void:
    var tile_set := TileSet.new()
    tile_set.tile_size = Vector2i(16, 16)
    tile_set.add_physics_layer()
    tile_set.set_physics_layer_collision_layer(0, 1 << 1)   # bit 2 ("walls")
    tile_set.add_custom_data_layer()
    tile_set.set_custom_data_layer_name(0, "damage")
    tile_set.set_custom_data_layer_type(0, TYPE_INT)

    var atlas := TileSetAtlasSource.new()
    atlas.texture = load("res://art/tiles.png")
    atlas.texture_region_size = Vector2i(16, 16)
    tile_set.add_source(atlas, 0)                  # add before creating tiles
    atlas.create_tile(Vector2i(2, 1))              # column 2, row 1 of the texture
    var wall := atlas.get_tile_data(Vector2i(2, 1), 0)
    wall.add_collision_polygon(0)
    wall.set_collision_polygon_points(0, 0, PackedVector2Array([
        Vector2(-8, -8), Vector2(8, -8), Vector2(8, 8), Vector2(-8, 8)]))  # cell-centred
    wall.set_custom_data("damage", 0)

    var err := ResourceSaver.save(tile_set, "res://tiles/world_tileset.tres")
    print("saved tileset: ", error_string(err))
    quit(0 if err == OK else 1)
```

skills.body:
---
name: godot-ui-control
description: >
  Godot 4.7 Control-node API for menus and HUDs: anchors, Containers, Theme and StyleBox, focus
  neighbours and stretch settings, with a headless layout check. Use when Godot UI overlaps or
  drifts on resize, buttons ignore the gamepad, or an invisible panel swallows clicks. Not for
  engine-neutral UI rules (`game-ui-ux`; load both) or rebinding (`input-systems`).
---

# Godot UI / Control nodes (4.x)

Lay out responsive UI with `Control` anchors and `Container` nodes, style it with a
`Theme`, make it navigable by keyboard and gamepad, and prove the layout holds at more
than one screen size. Targets **Godot 4.7** (see Version notes). Design rules (what a good
HUD or menu needs) live in `game-ui-ux`; load both for engine UI work.

## When to use

- HUDs, menus, inventories, dialog boxes or settings screens built from `Control` nodes;
  UI that must adapt to window size; theming; focus navigation for controller/keyboard.

**When *not* to use:** in-world `Node2D`/sprites → `godot-nodes-scenes`; UI tweens →
`godot-animation`; rebinding → `input-systems`; card hands and VN text boxes →
`card-game` / `visual-novel`.

## Core workflow

1. **Read the stretch settings first.** `project.godot` `[display]` holds
   `window/size/viewport_width`/`viewport_height` (base size, default 1152x648),
   `window/stretch/mode` (`canvas_items` is the usual choice for UI-heavy games) and
   `window/stretch/aspect` (`expand` lets UI use extra width or height). Layout bugs on
   other screens usually start here.
2. **Use `Control` nodes for UI**, not `Node2D`, and put HUDs under a `CanvasLayer` so the
   game camera does not move them.
3. **Anchor top-level panels; let Containers place their children.** Outside containers,
   set anchors with presets (`set_anchors_and_offsets_preset()`). Inside a `VBoxContainer`,
   `HBoxContainer`, `GridContainer` or `MarginContainer`, the container owns position and
   size; steer it with `size_flags_*`. In a `.tscn`, a Full Rect panel reads:

   ```ini
   [node name="PauseMenu" type="Control"]
   anchors_preset = 15
   anchor_right = 1.0
   anchor_bottom = 1.0
   grow_horizontal = 2
   grow_vertical = 2
   ```

   Keep whatever `layout_mode` line Godot wrote; it records whether anchors or a parent
   container drive the node.
4. **Style with one `Theme`.** Set a project-wide theme with `gui/theme/custom="res://ui/theme.tres"`
   in `project.godot`, or assign `theme` on the top Control; children inherit it. Use
   per-node `add_theme_*_override` only for exceptions.
5. **Wire focus.** Give the first button focus when a menu opens (`grab_focus()`), keep
   `focus_mode = FOCUS_ALL` on anything a gamepad must reach, and set
   `focus_neighbor_*` only where the automatic geometry guess is wrong.
6. **Connect signals** (`pressed`, `toggled`, `text_submitted`, `value_changed`).
7. **Check before you finish.**
   - Run the layout test (Pattern 4) headless:
     `godot --headless --path . --script res://tests/test_ui_layout.gd` and read the exit
     code. It flags controls pushed off-screen and menus with nothing focused, at each size.
   - Run the `godot-nodes-scenes` skill's `scripts/check_godot_project.py <project-dir>` if you edited
     `.tscn`/`.tres` files (themes, StyleBoxes, fonts).
   - For a picture, on a machine with a GPU (not `--headless`), capture frames and look
     at them: `godot --path . --resolution 2560x1080 --write-movie $OUT/menu.png --quit-after 3 --scene res://ui/main_menu.tscn`
     writes numbered PNGs next to that path. Repeat at 1280x720.
   - With no Godot binary (`godot`, `godot4` or `$GODOT_BIN`), ask the user to run these
     and paste the output or screenshots. Ask the user to try the menu with a gamepad
     and report any button that cannot be reached.

## Patterns

### 1. Full Rect from code (anchors *and* offsets)

```gdscript
extends Control

func _ready() -> void:
    # Setting only anchors (or `anchors_preset`) keeps the old offsets, so the rect
    # would not snap to the preset. This moves anchors AND resets offsets.
    set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
```

### 2. A menu from containers, with initial focus

```gdscript
extends VBoxContainer    # children stack vertically, auto-sized

func _ready() -> void:
    for child in get_children():
        if child is Button:
            child.pressed.connect(_on_button_pressed.bind(child.name))
    # Give the first button focus so a gamepad can navigate immediately.
    if get_child_count() > 0:
        (get_child(0) as Control).grab_focus()

func _on_button_pressed(which: StringName) -> void:
    match which:
        "PlayButton":  get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://game.tscn")
        "QuitButton":  get_tree().quit()
```

### 3. One child takes the leftover space

```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
    $Label.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_BEGIN
    $Spacer.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL   # grows to fill
```

### 4. Headless layout test at several sizes

```gdscript
# res://tests/test_ui_layout.gd
extends SceneTree

# The sizes the UI really gets. With stretch mode canvas_items and aspect "expand",
# a 2560x1080 window on a 1152x648 base gives the UI 1536x648, not 2560x1080.
const SIZES: Array[Vector2i] = [Vector2i(1152, 648), Vector2i(1536, 648), Vector2i(1152, 864)]

func _initialize() -> void:
    var failed := 0
    for size in SIZES:
        var vp := SubViewport.new()
        vp.size = size
        root.add_child(vp)
        var ui: Control = load("res://ui/main_menu.tscn").instantiate()
        vp.add_child(ui)
        await process_frame
        await process_frame                      # containers re-sort a frame later
        var screen := Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(size))
        for node in ui.find_children("*", "Control", true, false):
            var c := node as Control
            if c.is_visible_in_tree() and not screen.encloses(c.get_global_rect()):
                failed += 1
                push_error("%s off-screen at %s: %s" % [ui.get_path_to(c), size, c.get_global_rect()])
        if vp.gui_get_focus_owner() == null:
            failed += 1
            push_error("nothing has focus at %s, so a gamepad cannot navigate" % size)
        vp.free()
    print("Results: %d failed" % failed)
    quit(1 if failed > 0 else 0)
```

Children of a `ScrollContainer` are meant to extend past it; skip them (or check only the
container) when the menu scrolls.

## Gotchas

- **Mixing manual position with Containers.** A container child cannot keep its own
  position or anchors; the container overwrites them on every sort. To nudge, rotate or
  scale one (a hover pop), set `offset_transform_enabled = true` and use
  `offset_transform_position`/`_rotation`/`_scale`, which the container leaves alone.
- **Anchors vs offsets.** Anchors are fractions of the parent; offsets are pixels from the
  anchored point. Positioning with anchors at 0 makes UI ignore window size.
- **UI under a `Node2D`** doesn't theme, anchor or take focus correctly. Keep UI in a
  `Control` subtree, under a `CanvasLayer` for HUDs.
- **Gamepad does nothing** → nothing has focus. Call `grab_focus()` when the screen opens;
  plain `Control`s default to `FOCUS_NONE`, `FOCUS_CLICK` is mouse-only, and
  `grab_focus()` on a `FOCUS_NONE` control only prints a warning.
- **Invisible full-rect panel swallows clicks** → its `mouse_filter` is `STOP`. Set
  `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE` on decorative panels and HUD roots.
- **Looks right in the editor, cramped or off-screen on ultrawide or 4:3** → stretch
  `aspect` is `keep` (black bars) or the panel is anchored to a corner instead of the
  edge it should follow. Test the sizes the UI actually gets (Pattern 4).
- **Theme vs override.** Per-node `add_theme_*_override` calls beat the inherited `Theme`;
  many of them defeat central theming and make restyling slow.
- **`rect_*` properties are renamed.** Godot 3's `rect_size`/`rect_position`/`rect_min_size`
  are now `size`/`position`/`custom_minimum_size`.

## References

- Read `references/layout-and-theming.md` when you need the anchor/offset maths, every
  Container type, size-flag values, building a Theme and StyleBox in code, focus neighbour
  wiring, offset transforms, the built-in `VirtualJoystick`, or common Control signals.

## Related skills

- `game-ui-ux` for engine-neutral rules: scaling, safe areas, focus flow, screen stack.
- `godot-animation` for Tween-based UI transitions.
- `godot-signals-groups` for wiring UI events to game logic.
- `input-systems` for rebindable input and multi-device focus.
- `card-game` / `visual-novel` for UI-heavy genre templates.

## Version notes

Last verified: 2026-11-11 against Godot 4.7.2-stable (released 2026-08-18).

- `Control.offset_transform_*` and the `VirtualJoystick` node are new in 4.7.
- Default base size is 1152x648 and default stretch mode is `disabled`, aspect `keep`.
- `--write-movie` with a `.png` path writes an image sequence; `--resolution` requests the
  window size.

Sources: [Control @ 4.7.2-stable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/doc/classes/Control.xml),
[ProjectSettings @ 4.7.2-stable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/doc/classes/ProjectSettings.xml),
[main.cpp @ 4.7.2-stable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/main/main.cpp),
[Multiple resolutions](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/rendering/multiple_resolutions.html),
[Godot 4.7 release](https://godotengine.org/releases/4.7).

     writes numbered PNGs next to that path. Repeat at 1280x720.
   - With no Godot binary (`godot`, `godot4` or `$GODOT_BIN`), ask the user to run these
     and paste the output or screenshots. Ask the user to try the menu with a gamepad
     and report any button that cannot be reached.

## Patterns

### 1. Full Rect from code (anchors *and* offsets)

```gdscript
extends Control

func _ready() -> void:
    # Setting only anchors (or `anchors_preset`) keeps the old offsets, so the rect
    # would not snap to the preset. This moves anchors AND resets offsets.
    set_anchors_and_offsets_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
```

### 2. A menu from containers, with initial focus

```gdscript
extends VBoxContainer    # children stack vertically, auto-sized

func _ready() -> void:
    for child in get_children():
        if child is Button:
            child.pressed.connect(_on_button_pressed.bind(child.name))
    # Give the first button focus so a gamepad can navigate immediately.
    if get_child_count() > 0:
        (get_child(0) as Control).grab_focus()

func _on_button_pressed(which: StringName) -> void:
    match which:
        "PlayButton":  get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://game.tscn")
        "QuitButton":  get_tree().quit()
```

### 3. One child takes the leftover space

```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
    $Label.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_BEGIN
    $Spacer.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL   # grows to fill
```

### 4. Headless layout test at several sizes

```gdscript
# res://tests/test_ui_layout.gd
extends SceneTree

# The sizes the UI really gets. With stretch mode canvas_items and aspect "expand",
# a 2560x1080 window on a 1152x648 base gives the UI 1536x648, not 2560x1080.
const SIZES: Array[Vector2i] = [Vector2i(1152, 648), Vector2i(1536, 648), Vector2i(1152, 864)]

func _initialize() -> void:
    var failed := 0
    for size in SIZES:
        var vp := SubViewport.new()
        vp.size = size
        root.add_child(vp)
        var ui: Control = load("res://ui/main_menu.tscn").instantiate()
        vp.add_child(ui)
        await process_frame
        await process_frame                      # containers re-sort a frame later
        var screen := Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(size))
        for node in ui.find_children("*", "Control", true, false):
            var c := node as Control
            if c.is_visible_in_tree() and not screen.encloses(c.get_global_rect()):
                failed += 1
                push_error("%s off-screen at %s: %s" % [ui.get_path_to(c), size, c.get_global_rect()])
        if vp.gui_get_focus_owner() == null:
            failed += 1
            push_error("nothing has focus at %s, so a gamepad cannot navigate" % size)
        vp.free()
    print("Results: %d failed" % failed)
    quit(1 if failed > 0 else 0)
```

Children of a `ScrollContainer` are meant to extend past it; skip them (or check only the
container) when the menu scrolls.

## Gotchas

- **Mixing manual position with Containers.** A container child cannot keep its own
  position or anchors; the container overwrites them on every sort. To nudge, rotate or
  scale one (a hover pop), set `offset_transform_enabled = true` and use
  `offset_transform_position`/`_rotation`/`_scale`, which the container leaves alone.
- **Anchors vs offsets.** Anchors are fractions of the parent; offsets are pixels from the
  anchored point. Positioning with anchors at 0 makes UI ignore window size.
- **UI under a `Node2D`** doesn't theme, anchor or take focus correctly. Keep UI in a
  `Control` subtree, under a `CanvasLayer` for HUDs.
- **Gamepad does nothing** → nothing has focus. Call `grab_focus()` when the screen opens;
  plain `Control`s default to `FOCUS_NONE`, `FOCUS_CLICK` is mouse-only, and
  `grab_focus()` on a `FOCUS_NONE` control only prints a warning.
- **Invisible full-rect panel swallows clicks** → its `mouse_filter` is `STOP`. Set
  `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE` on decorative panels and HUD roots.
- **Looks right in the editor, cramped or off-screen on ultrawide or 4:3** → stretch
  `aspect` is `keep` (black bars) or the panel is anchored to a corner instead of the
  edge it should follow. Test the sizes the UI actually gets (Pattern 4).
- **Theme vs override.** Per-node `add_theme_*_override` calls beat the inherited `Theme`;
  many of them defeat central theming and make restyling slow.
- **`rect_*` properties are renamed.** Godot 3's `rect_size`/`rect_position`/`rect_min_size`
  are now `size`/`position`/`custom_minimum_size`.

## References

- Read `references/layout-and-theming.md` when you need the anchor/offset maths, every
  Container type, size-flag values, building a Theme and StyleBox in code, focus neighbour
  wiring, offset transforms, the built-in `VirtualJoystick`, or common Control signals.

- `game-ui-ux` for engine-neutral rules: scaling, safe areas, focus flow, screen stack.

- `input-systems` for rebindable input and multi-device focus.
- `card-game` / `visual-novel` for UI-heavy genre templates.

## Version notes

Last verified: 2026-11-11 against Godot 4.7.2-stable (released 2026-08-18).

- `Control.offset_transform_*` and the `VirtualJoystick` node are new in 4.7.
- Default base size is 1152x648 and default stretch mode is `disabled`, aspect `keep`.

  window size.

Sources: [Control @ 4.7.2-stable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/doc/classes/Control.xml),
[ProjectSettings @ 4.7.2-stable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/doc/classes/ProjectSettings.xml),
[main.cpp @ 4.7.2-stable](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/main/main.cpp),

skills.body:
---
name: bevy-ecs
description: >
  Builds and debugs Bevy 0.20 games in Rust: components, Query and Commands systems, schedules,
  States, observers and headless tests. Use when Cargo.toml depends on bevy, on a B0001
  query-conflict panic, or pre-0.20 code (EventReader, SpriteBundle). Not for engine-neutral AI,
  generation, physics or shaders (`game-ai`, `procedural-gen`, `physics-tuning`,
  `shader-programming`).
---

# Bevy ECS

Structure and debug a Bevy game around its ECS. New code targets **Bevy 0.20** (`bevy =
"0.20"`, which resolves to the latest 0.20.x patch). Bevy breaks APIs in every minor
release, so the version the project pins decides which syntax is right.

## When to use

- Wiring an `App`, defining components and resources, writing systems, ordering them,
  gating them on state or timers, or passing data with messages and observers.
- Fixing query-conflict panics, entities that seem missing, order bugs, or code copied from
  an older Bevy release.

**When not to use:** rendering pipelines, custom shaders, UI layout and audio are outside
this skill; AI and generation algorithms go to `game-ai` / `procedural-gen`.

## Workflow

1. **Read the pinned version first.** `Cargo.toml` gives the requirement and `Cargo.lock`
   the resolved `bevy` version. Keep it; a minor-release migration is a separate task that
   follows that release's migration guide. Never mix snippets from two minors.
2. **Model the data.** Per-entity data is a `#[derive(Component)]`; one-of-a-kind data
   (score, settings) is a `#[derive(Resource)]`. Spawn entities as tuples of components;
   required components fill in the rest (`commands.spawn(Camera2d)` adds `Transform`,
   `Camera` and friends).
3. **Write systems as plain functions** whose parameters declare access: `Query<D, F>`,
   `Res`/`ResMut`, `Commands`, `MessageReader`/`MessageWriter`, `Single`. Systems with
   non-conflicting access run in parallel, in no guaranteed order.
4. **Order only what must be ordered** (`.chain()`, `.before`/`.after`, `SystemSet`s) and
   gate with `run_if`. Group features into `Plugin`s. Scale motion by `time.delta_secs()`
   or put it in `FixedUpdate`.
5. **Verify.** Run `cargo check`, then `cargo test` with a headless `App` test (pattern
   below) for each rule you changed, then `cargo run` and read the first panic: Bevy
   reports conflicting system parameters when a schedule first runs, with an error code
   and a link. Report which of these you ran; a clean `cargo check` proves only that it
   compiles. When the change is visual, ask the user to run the game and report what they
   see.

## Patterns

### Spawning and filtering

```rust
#[derive(Component)]
struct Player;
#[derive(Component)]
struct Velocity(Vec2);

fn setup(mut commands: Commands) {
    commands.spawn(Camera2d);
    commands.spawn((Player, Velocity(Vec2::new(150.0, 0.0)), Transform::default()));
}

fn move_players(time: Res<Time>, mut q: Query<(&Velocity, &mut Transform)>) {
    for (v, mut t) in &mut q {
        t.translation += v.0.extend(0.0) * time.delta_secs();
    }
}

// Two &mut Transform queries in one system must be provably disjoint.
fn separate(
    mut players: Query<&mut Transform, With<Player>>,
    mut others: Query<&mut Transform, Without<Player>>,
) { /* ... */ }
```

### Ordering, run conditions, plugins

```rust
struct GameplayPlugin;
impl Plugin for GameplayPlugin {
    fn build(&self, app: &mut App) {
        app.insert_resource(Score(0))
            .add_systems(Startup, setup)
            // damage must resolve before deaths are checked
            .add_systems(Update, (apply_damage, check_deaths).chain())
            .add_systems(Update, spawn_wave.run_if(in_state(AppState::Playing)));
    }
}
```

### Headless test (the check to run)

`MinimalPlugins` gives time and a schedule runner with no window or GPU, so this runs under
plain `cargo test`. Drive time by hand to make movement deterministic.

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use bevy::time::TimeUpdateStrategy;
    use std::time::Duration;

    #[test]
    fn player_moves_at_its_velocity() {
        let mut app = App::new();
        app.add_plugins(MinimalPlugins)
            .insert_resource(TimeUpdateStrategy::ManualDuration(Duration::from_millis(100)))
            .add_systems(Update, move_players);
        let id = app.world_mut().spawn((Velocity(Vec2::X * 10.0), Transform::default())).id();
        for _ in 0..5 {
            app.update();
        }
        // The first update has a zero delta, so 5 updates advance 4 x 0.1 s.
        let x = app.world().get::<Transform>(id).unwrap().translation.x;
        assert!((x - 4.0).abs() < 1e-4, "x = {x}");
    }
}
```

For whole-world assertions use `app.world_mut().query_filtered::<&Health, With<Player>>()`
and `.single(world)`. States need `bevy::state::app::StatesPlugin` next to `MinimalPlugins`.

## Gotchas

- **Panic `error[B0001]: Query<…> in system … accesses component(s) Transform in a way
  that conflicts with a previous system parameter`** → two queries in one system can both
  reach the same component mutably. Make them disjoint with `With`/`Without`, or use
  `ParamSet`.
- **`Query<EntityMut>` (or a broad `Query<Entity>` despawn loop) next to a `Res<T>`
  panics** → since 0.19 every resource lives on an entity tagged `IsResource`, so broad
  queries match resources too. The error is `B0002` when the `Res` comes after the query
  and `B0001` when it comes first. Query your own marker, or add `Without<IsResource>`
  (`use bevy::ecs::resource::IsResource`).
- **"conflicting implementations of trait `Component`"** after deriving `Resource` and
  `Component` on one type → since 0.19 `Resource` implies `Component`; derive `Resource`
  alone.
- **A spawned entity is missing from a query in the same system** → `Commands` are
  deferred to the next sync point. Read it in a later system, or order the reader after
  the spawner.
- **Something works only by luck of system order** → unordered systems run in an
  arbitrary but stable order, which an unrelated change can reshuffle. Add a real
  constraint, and shake out hidden ones in tests with `ScheduleBuildSettings::shuffle_seed`
  (0.20, `debug` feature; see the reference).
- **Headless test sees no movement on the first update** → the first `app.update()` has a
  zero delta. Run one extra update or assert on N−1 steps, as in the test above.
- **`delta_seconds()` not found** → renamed to `delta_secs()` / `elapsed_secs()` in 0.15;
  the old names are gone.
- **`Camera2dBundle` / `SpriteBundle` not found** → bundles were removed in 0.16. Spawn
  the components (`Camera2d`, `Sprite`, `Transform`) and let required components fill in.
- **`EventReader` / `EventWriter` / `add_event` not found** → buffered events became
  messages: `#[derive(Message)]`, `MessageReader`, `MessageWriter::write`,
  `app.add_message::<T>()`. Push-style events use `#[derive(Event)]` with observers.
- **`On<Add, Player>`: "struct takes 1 generic argument but 2 generic arguments were
  supplied"** → 0.20 moved the component into the lifecycle event: `On<Add<Player>>`
  (also `Insert<T>`, `Discard<T>`, `Remove<T>`, `Despawn<T>`).
- **`Pointer<Click>` not found in a picking observer** → 0.20 flattened pointer events:
  observe `On<PointerClick>` / `On<PointerPress>` and read `click.pointer.position`
  (a `Vec2`).
- **`OnExit`/`OnEnter` run when "switching" to the current state** → `NextState::set`
  always transitions. Use `set_if_different` (0.20 name). The old `set_if_neq` now
  resolves to an unrelated change-detection method and fails with "can't compare
  `NextState<S>`".
- **"`text` does not live long enough" from `Name::new(text.as_str())`** → since 0.20
  `Name` takes a `&'static str` or an owned `String`: `Name::new(format!("Enemy {id}"))`.
- **Overlapping sprites swap draw order after moving to 0.20** → sprites render through the
  `Mesh2d` path and equal-`z` order was never guaranteed. Give overlapping sprites distinct
  `z` values.

## References

- Read `references/queries-and-scheduling.md` when the task needs more than the patterns
  above: query filters and `single()`, `iter_many` results, `ParamSet`, schedules and
  `SystemSet`s, 0.20 weak ordering and schedule shuffling, `States` with `DespawnOnExit`,
  change detection and summary ticks, the `Commands` lifecycle and `despawn_all`, exclusive
  `&mut World` systems, and message/observer syntax.

## Related skills

- `game-ai`, `procedural-gen` — portable algorithms to implement as systems.
- `physics-tuning` — fixed-step and collision feel; `shader-programming` — shader technique.
- `pygame-core`, `love2d-core` — lighter engines for small projects.

## Version notes

Last verified: 2026-11-11.

- Bevy 0.20.0 shipped on 2026-10-08 and 0.20.1 on 2026-10-28. 0.20.1 is a maintenance
  release (bug fixes, no API changes this skill relies on); 0.19.0 shipped 2026-06-19.
- Every 0.20 API in this skill and its reference, the panic texts in Gotchas and the
  headless test were compiled and run against `bevy = "=0.20.1"` (default features off,
  `bevy_state`, `bevy_log`, `debug`) with Rust 1.99. `Camera2d`, `Sprite` and pointer
  events were checked against the release notes and migration guide only.
- Sources: [crates.io bevy](https://crates.io/crates/bevy),
  [v0.20.1 release](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/releases/tag/v0.20.1),
  [Bevy 0.20 release notes](https://bevy.org/news/bevy-0-20/),
  [0.19 to 0.20 migration guide](https://bevy.org/learn/migration-guides/0-19-to-0-20/).

---
name: defold-core
description: >
  Builds and debugs Defold 1.14 games in Lua: collections, game objects, input focus, msg.post
  messaging, factories, collection proxies and Bob builds. Use for .collection or .script files,
  on_input never firing, a proxy that never loads, or "could not be found when dispatching

---

# Defold Core

Structure, wire and verify a Defold game: editor resource files, the Lua script lifecycle,
addressing and messages, runtime spawning and world loading, and a Bob build-and-run check.
Examples target **Defold 1.14.1**; they were built with Bob 1.14.1 and run on the 1.14.1
headless engine. An existing project keeps its Defold version (see [Version](#version)).

## When to use

- Use when adding or fixing game objects, collections, scripts, input, messages, spawning or
  level loading in a Defold project (`game.project` in the root, `.collection`, `.go`,
  `.script`, `.gui_script` files), or when Bob reports a missing resource.

**When *not* to use:** plain Lua or LÖVE projects (`love2d-core`); GUI layout, sprites,
tilemaps and physics depth beyond the pointers in the references; engine-agnostic design
handled by the related skills below.

## Workflow

1. **Inspect first.** Read `game.project` (`[bootstrap] main_collection`, `[input]
   game_binding`, `[project] dependencies`), the main collection, and the scripts near the
   request. Follow the project's folder layout, id naming and message names; do not
   reorganize. Note which Defold/Bob version CI or the team uses.
2. **Edit the right file type.** Game objects (`.go`) hold components; collections
   (`.collection`) place game objects and other collections; logic goes in `.script`
   (game objects), `.gui_script` (GUI) or shared `.lua` modules. Editor files are
   protobuf text: keep their structure, and copy shapes from
   `references/file-formats.md` instead of guessing fields.
3. **Check references.** Run `python scripts/check_defold_project.py <project-dir>` (path
   relative to this skill folder; Python 3.10+, no Defold install needed). Fix every `ERROR`
   (missing or wrong-case `/paths`, a `game.project` path without the compiled `c` suffix,
   a `require` whose file does not exist). Warnings cover files nothing uses yet, unfetched
   library dependencies and runtime-loaded files. Re-run until it exits 0.
4. **Build with Bob.** `java -jar bob.jar --root . --variant headless --archive resolve
   build` needs JDK 25 and a `bob.jar` matching the project's Defold version. Exit 1 plus
   an `ERROR:` line means a broken reference or a Lua syntax error (with file and line);
   `references/file-formats.md` shows how to trace an error that names a generated file.
5. **Run it.** A build does not prove the game works. Run a headless bundle under a timeout
   (`references/build-and-run.md`) and read the log: `ERROR:SCRIPT:` lines are Lua runtime
   errors, `ERROR:GAMEOBJECT:` lines bad addresses or socket clashes. Require a line your
   test prints when it finishes; the exit code alone proves nothing. The headless engine has
   no keyboard, mouse or screen, so for input, rendering or layout changes ask the user to
   run the game (editor **Project ▸ Build**, or the desktop bundle from the reference) and
   report what they see, and say what you could not verify.

## Patterns

### Project and resource references

`game.project` is an INI file in the project root. Resource paths everywhere are
root-absolute (`/main/player.go`). In `game.project` they name the **compiled** file, so the
source path gets a trailing `c`:

```ini
[bootstrap]
main_collection = /main/main.collectionc

[input]
game_binding = /input/game.input_bindingc
```

Bob builds only what is reachable from `game.project`; `/builtins/...` ships with the engine.

### Collections, game objects, components

A collection places instances and can override script properties per instance; a game object
lists file components and embedded components (escaped `data:` strings). Full verified
files are in `references/file-formats.md`.

```text
# main.collection (excerpt): place player.go and override its script's speed
instances {
  id: "player"
  prototype: "/main/player.go"
  component_properties {
    id: "player"
    properties { id: "speed" value: "250.0" type: PROPERTY_TYPE_NUMBER }
  }
}
```

### Script lifecycle, `self` and properties

```lua
go.property("speed", 200)                   -- top level only, literal default; editable per instance

local LEFT = hash("left")                   -- hash ids once, not every frame
local RIGHT = hash("right")
local FIRE = hash("fire")

function init(self)
	msg.post(".", "acquire_input_focus")    -- no focus, no on_input calls
	self.held = {}                          -- per-instance state lives on self
end

function update(self, dt)
	local dir = (self.held[RIGHT] and 1 or 0) - (self.held[LEFT] and 1 or 0)
	if dir ~= 0 then
		local pos = go.get_position()
		pos.x = pos.x + dir * self.speed * dt    -- dt-scaled: same speed at any frame rate
		go.set_position(pos)
	end
end

function on_input(self, action_id, action)
	if action_id == LEFT or action_id == RIGHT then
		if action.pressed then self.held[action_id] = true
		elseif action.released then self.held[action_id] = nil end
		return true                         -- consumed: listeners lower on the stack skip it
	elseif action_id == FIRE and action.pressed then
		factory.create("#bulletfactory", go.get_position(), nil,
			{ velocity = vmath.vector3(0, 600, 0) })
		return true
	end
end

function final(self)
	msg.post(".", "release_input_focus")
end
```

Callbacks: `init`, `final`, `fixed_update`, `update`, `late_update` (after every `update`,
before render), `on_message`, `on_input`, `on_reload`. Update order between game
objects is unspecified. `fixed_update` runs 0..N times per frame at `[engine]
fixed_update_frequency`; set `[physics] use_fixed_timestep = 1` too so physics steps at the
same rate, and put physics-driven code there. `self` is userdata: store
fields on it, but `pairs(self)` and `pprint(self)` do not work. Property types: number,
boolean, hash, `msg.url`, `vmath.vector3`/`vector4`, `vmath.quat`, resources such as
`resource.atlas("/main/main.atlas")`, and (since 1.13.2) strings.

### Input bindings and the input stack

`.input_binding` maps devices to action names (`key_trigger`, `mouse_trigger`, plus
gamepad, touch and text triggers). Every component that acquired focus sits on an input
stack; the last to acquire is on top and gets input first, and returning `true` from
`on_input` stops it there, which is how pause menus block gameplay input. Key actions report
`pressed` and `released`; track held keys yourself as above. Since 1.14.1, `action.source`
is a hash (`mouse`, `touch`, `keyboard`, `gamepad`, `text` or `accelerometer`), which tells a
real mouse click from one simulated by touch.

### Addressing and messages

A URL is `[socket:][path][#fragment]`: `"."` is this game object, `"#"` this component,
`"#sprite"` a sibling component, `"enemy#ai"` a relative object, `"/manager#controller"` an
absolute one, `"main:/loader#loader"` an object in another world. Collections create naming
scopes, so a string id is resolved relative to the sender's collection; a pre-hashed id is
always absolute.

```lua
msg.post("/manager#controller", "enemy_spotted", { id = go.get_id() })

function on_message(self, message_id, message, sender)
	if message_id == hash("enemy_spotted") then
		print("from", sender, "id", message.id)
	end
end
```

Messages are queued and dispatched later in the frame; the table is capped at 2 KB. A bad
address logs `ERROR:GAMEOBJECT: Instance '/x' could not be found when dispatching message`.

### Factories and collection factories

```lua
-- factory component "#bulletfactory" -> one game object; properties override go.property values
local id = factory.create("#bulletfactory", pos, nil, { velocity = vmath.vector3(0, 600, 0) })

-- collectionfactory component "#wavefactory" -> table of collection ids -> new instance ids
local ids = collectionfactory.create("#wavefactory", vmath.vector3(480, 500, 0))
local leader = ids[hash("/leader")]         -- e.g. hash: [/collection0/leader]
go.delete(ids, true)                        -- later: delete them and their children
```

Position and rotation default to the spawning object's. `go.delete()` takes effect at the
end of the frame. Per-instance properties for a collection factory are keyed by id:
`{ [hash("/leader")] = { hp = 5 } }`.

### Collection proxies (load another world)

```lua
-- excerpt from the loader script; the collection's "#levelproxy" component is a collectionproxy
function init(self)
	msg.post(".", "acquire_input_focus")        -- else the loaded world gets no input
	msg.post("#levelproxy", "async_load")       -- or "load"
end

function on_message(self, message_id, message, sender)
	if message_id == hash("proxy_loaded") then
		msg.post(sender, "init")
		msg.post(sender, "enable")
	elseif message_id == hash("level_done") then
		msg.post("#levelproxy", "unload")       -- disables and finalizes first
	elseif message_id == hash("proxy_unloaded") then
		-- safe to load the next level here
	end
end
```

The loaded world's socket is the **`name:` of the loaded collection file**, so scripts in it
reply with `msg.post("main:/loader#loader", ...)` and its own URLs read
`level1:/level#level`. `set_time_step { factor = 0, mode = 0 }` pauses a proxy world.

## Version

`game.project` has no engine version key. Use the Defold editor or `bob.jar` version the
project is built with (CI often pins a release sha1), and `library.defold_min_version` when the
project is a library. `java -jar bob.jar --version` prints the version and sha1. Keep that
version; do not migrate unless asked.

## Gotchas

- **Bob: `the bootstrap.main_collection '/main/main.collectio' can't be found`** → the
  setting lacks the compiled suffix and Bob stripped the last letter. Write
  `/main/main.collectionc` (same for `input.game_binding` → `.input_bindingc`).
- **Bob: `ERROR: build/default/_generated_….factory:0: the prototype '/main/x.go' can't be
  found`** → an embedded component in some `.go` points at a missing file. Search the
  sources for the quoted path (`/main/x.go`), not the generated name, or run the checker.
- **`on_input` never fires** → the object never sent `acquire_input_focus`, the action name
  differs from the binding, `input.game_binding` points elsewhere, or a listener higher on
  the stack returns `true`.
- **Input dead inside a proxy-loaded level** → the game object holding the collection proxy
  did not acquire input focus.
- **`already a socket with the same name` and the proxy never sends `proxy_loaded`** → the
  loaded collection's `name:` equals an already loaded world (often both are `"main"` or
  `"default"`). Give every proxied collection a unique name.
- **`fixed_update` never runs** → `[engine] fixed_update_frequency` is 0 (default 60). For
  physics also set `[physics] use_fixed_timestep = 1`, as the manual requires both.
- **`module 'modules.util' not found` at run time although Bob succeeded** → a `require` used
  slashes (`require "modules/util"`). Use the dotted path from the project root,
  `require "modules.util"` for `/modules/util.lua`.
- **An HTML5 build shows a black screen or shader errors only on old WebGL 1 devices, after
  moving to 1.14.1** → 1.14.1 stopped compiling GLES 2.0 / WebGL 1 shaders by default. Set
  `[shader] exclude_gles_sm100 = 0` in `game.project` if the game must still run there.
- **Bob fails at once with `UnsupportedClassVersionError … class file version 69.0`** →
  Bob 1.14.x needs Java 25; an older JDK is on the `PATH`.
- **`tostring(id)` prints `hash: [<unknown:…>]`** → hashes keep their source text only in
  debug builds. Compare hashes, never their strings.
- **A second engine logs `Failed to initialize Remotery`, or a test run never ends** → the
  debug engine opens an engine service (port 8001), a log server and a profiler port, and
  waits forever without `sys.exit`. Run one engine at a time and always use a timeout.

## References

- Read `references/file-formats.md` before writing or repairing editor files by hand, or
  when a Bob error names a generated file: verified minimal `game.project`, `.collection`,
  `.go`, `.atlas`, `.input_binding` and script files, and how to trace errors to a source.
- Read `references/build-and-run.md` when you build, bundle or smoke-test: Java and
  `bob.jar` downloads, Bob commands, platforms and variants, the headless smoke test with
  timeout and log checks, ports, and manual pointers for GUI, sprites, tilemaps and
  collision objects.
- Run `scripts/check_defold_project.py` after editing resource files (workflow step 3);
  `--help` lists every check.

## Related skills

- `input-systems` — rebinding, gamepad support and buffering on top of Defold bindings.
- `game-ui-ux` — HUD and menu design to build with GUI scenes and `.gui_script`.
- `physics-tuning` — fixed-timestep and collision tuning for collision objects.
- `camera-systems` — follow/deadzone logic, typically applied in `late_update`.
- `save-systems` — save formats and slots; pair with Defold's `sys.save`/`sys.load`.
- `game-feel` — juice built from `go.animate` and timers.
- `platformer`, `level-design` — genre and layout guidance that binds to this skill.
- `love2d-core` — the other Lua engine in this catalog, for LÖVE projects.

## Version notes

Last verified: 2026-11-11.

- Defold 1.14.1 became the stable release on 2026-11-10 (sha1
  `ee283d4dad9fa451dd6399d83602e1dc25133681`); 1.14.0 was released on 2026-10-12.
- 1.14.1 changes that touch this skill: GLES 2.0 / WebGL 1 shaders are excluded by default
  (`[shader] exclude_gles_sm100` now defaults to 1), `action.source` in `on_input`, and the
  debug and headless engines print an OpenAPI URL for their engine service at startup.
- Bob 1.14.1 needs OpenJDK 25 (its classes are version 69).
- The example project in the references (player, factory, collection factory, proxy-loaded
  level), the smoke bundle and the quoted build and runtime errors were rebuilt with Bob
  1.14.1 and run on the 1.14.1 `dmengine_headless` with Temurin 25.0.5 on Linux x86_64.
  `action.source` was not run (the headless engine has no input); it comes from the
  release notes.
- Sources: [stable info.json](https://d.defold.com/stable/info.json),
  [1.14.1 release](https://github.com/defold/defold/releases/tag/1.14.1),
  [1.14.1 release notes (beta post)](https://forum.defold.com/t/defold-1-14-1-beta/83389),
  [GLES 2.0 default change (PR #13543)](https://github.com/defold/defold/pull/13543),
  [Bob manual](https://defold.com/manuals/bob/).

skills.body:
---
name: love2d-core
description: >
  Builds and debugs LÖVE (Love2D) 11.x games in Lua: main.lua callbacks, conf.lua, fixed steps,
  crisp pixel-art scaling, love.filesystem saves and a scripted run. Use when main.lua calls
  love.*, or on blurry pixel art, the blue error screen or speed tied to frame rate. Not for
  Defold (`defold-core`) or engine-neutral saves and input (`save-systems`, `input-systems`).
---

# LÖVE (Love2D) Core

Build and debug a LÖVE game. New code targets **LÖVE 11.5**, the current stable release;
12.0 is unreleased and changes APIs, so do not copy 12.0 examples into an 11.x game.

## When to use

- Starting a LÖVE game, or fixing its loop, timing, input, drawing, scaling, saving or
  screen flow.
- Any folder with `main.lua` calling `love.*`, a `conf.lua`, or a `.love` archive.

**When not to use:** Defold (also Lua, but `game.project` and `.script` files); physics
joints, shaders and networking beyond pointers; portable design owned by related skills.

## Workflow

1. **Read `conf.lua` first.** `t.version` names the target LÖVE version and `t.identity`
   the save folder. Keep the project's version; ask before porting between 0.10, 11 and 12.
2. **Load once, draw often.** Create images, fonts, canvases and sounds in `love.load` (or
   a loader), never inside `love.draw` or `love.update`.
3. **Simulate in steps.** Scale motion by `dt`; for physics, collisions or replays use the
   fixed-step accumulator below.
4. **Wrap world drawing in `push`/`pop`** and draw the HUD after `pop`, in screen space.
5. **Verify.** Add the `--frames` check below and run it under a timeout; read the output
   and open the screenshot in the save directory. Report what you ran. Input feel and sound
   need a person: ask the user to play briefly and report speed, controls and audio.

## Pattern: conf.lua with an error-exit hook

```lua
function love.conf(t)
    t.version = "11.5"               -- warns when run on another LÖVE version
    t.identity = "my-game"           -- save folder name; set it before the first release
    t.window.width, t.window.height = 960, 540
end

-- Under --frames, print errors and exit 1 instead of showing the blue error screen.
-- conf.lua runs before main.lua, so this also catches syntax errors in main.lua.
if arg and table.concat(arg, " "):find("--frames", 1, true) then
    function love.errorhandler(msg)
        print("ERROR: " .. tostring(msg) .. debug.traceback("", 2))
        return function() return 1 end
    end
end
```

## Pattern: fixed step and a scripted run

```lua
local STEP = 1 / 60
local acc = 0
local check = { frames = nil, shot = nil, count = 0 }
local player

function love.load(args)             -- args: command-line arguments after the game folder
    for i, a in ipairs(args) do
        if a == "--frames" then check.frames = tonumber(args[i + 1]) end
        if a == "--shot" then check.shot = args[i + 1] end
    end
    love.graphics.setDefaultFilter("nearest", "nearest")  -- before any newImage/newCanvas
    player = { x = 100, y = 100, speed = 120 }            -- pixels per second
end

local function step(dt)
    local dx = (love.keyboard.isDown("right") and 1 or 0)
             - (love.keyboard.isDown("left") and 1 or 0)
    player.x = player.x + dx * player.speed * dt
end

function love.update(dt)
    acc = acc + math.min(dt, 0.25)   -- clamp stalls so the loop cannot spiral
    while acc >= STEP do
        step(STEP)
        acc = acc - STEP
    end
    check.count = check.count + 1
    if check.frames and check.count == check.frames and check.shot then
        love.graphics.captureScreenshot(check.shot)       -- saved in the save directory
    elseif check.frames and check.count > check.frames then
        print("RUN OK frames=" .. check.frames .. " save=" .. love.filesystem.getSaveDirectory())
        love.event.quit(0)
    end
end
```

Use `love.keypressed(key, scancode, isrepeat)` for one-off actions and
`love.keyboard.isDown` inside `step` for held movement.

## Pattern: pixel-art canvas and camera

```lua
local W, H = 320, 180
local canvas                         -- create in love.load, after setDefaultFilter

function love.draw()
    love.graphics.setCanvas(canvas)
    love.graphics.clear(0.1, 0.1, 0.12)
    love.graphics.push()
    love.graphics.translate(-math.floor(cam.x), -math.floor(cam.y))  -- whole pixels
    drawWorld()
    love.graphics.pop()              -- every push needs a pop, even on an early return
    drawHud()                        -- screen space, after pop
    love.graphics.setCanvas()

    local w, h = love.graphics.getDimensions()
    local s = math.max(1, math.floor(math.min(w / W, h / H)))  -- integer scale only
    love.graphics.draw(canvas, math.floor((w - W * s) / 2), math.floor((h - H * s) / 2), 0, s, s)
end
```

Save with `love.filesystem.write("save.lua", text)` and read back with
`love.filesystem.read` or `love.filesystem.load`; files land in the save directory.

## The check to run

```sh
love --version
timeout 30 love . --frames 120 --shot frame.png; echo "exit=$?"
```

Expect `RUN OK` and exit 0; exit 1 prints the Lua error and traceback; exit 124 means the
game hung or the error hook is missing. The PNG is in the printed save directory, not the
project folder. On a Linux machine without a display, run `xvfb-run -a love . …`; if OpenAL
cannot open a sound device there, point `ALSA_CONFIG_PATH` at a file containing
`pcm.!default { type null }`.

## Gotchas

- **Pixel art looks blurry** → images default to linear filtering. Call
  `love.graphics.setDefaultFilter("nearest", "nearest")` before creating images, fonts or
  canvases (earlier objects keep `linear`), draw to a low-resolution canvas, scale it by a
  whole number, and round camera offsets.
- **`Maximum stack depth reached (more pushes than pops?)`** → a `push` without a matching
  `pop`, often skipped by an early `return` in `love.draw`. The stack survives across frames,
  so the error appears a few frames later. `Minimum stack depth reached` is the reverse.
- **Save file missing from the project folder** → `love.filesystem.write` only writes to the
  save directory (`love.filesystem.getSaveDirectory()`, named by `t.identity`; on Linux
  `~/.local/share/love/<identity>`). The game folder is read-only. Changing `t.identity`
  after release orphans players' saves.
- **A module's state resets or is duplicated** → it was required with two spellings.
  `require("screens.menu")` and `require("screens/menu")` load two separate copies. Always
  use dotted paths from the game root.
- **Same "random" level every run** → LuaJIT's `math.random` is not seeded at startup, while
  `love.math.random` is. Use `love.math.random` (or `love.math.newRandomGenerator(seed)` for
  replayable runs).
- **Speed changes with frame rate, or objects tunnel after a stall** → scale by `dt`, clamp
  `dt`, and step physics and collisions at a fixed rate.
- **The game freezes on the blue error screen in a scripted run** → the default error
  handler waits for the user. Use the `conf.lua` hook above so errors print and exit 1.
- **Colours come out white or fully opaque** → 11.x colours are 0–1. `setColor(128, 234,
  255)` draws white; use `love.math.colorFromBytes(128, 234, 255)` for byte values.
- **Everything is tinted after one `setColor`** → colour is global state. Reset with
  `love.graphics.setColor(1, 1, 1)` before drawing images and text.
- **`love.conf` has no effect** → it must be in `conf.lua`, which runs before `main.lua`.
- **Holding a key fires `love.keypressed` once** → key repeat is off by default.
  `love.keyboard.setKeyRepeat(true)` enables it; repeats arrive with `isrepeat == true`.
- **Memory climbs and frames slow down** → `newFont`, `newImage` or `newCanvas` is called
  every frame. Create them once and reuse them.

## References

- Read `references/state-stack.md` when the game needs menus, pause overlays or several
  screens: a complete push/pop screen manager with delegated callbacks and example screens.

## Related skills

- `save-systems` — save formats, slots and migration; `input-systems` — rebinding and
  gamepads.
- `defold-core` — the other Lua engine in this catalog; `pygame-core` — the same loop in
  Python.

## Version notes

Last verified: 2026-11-11.

- LÖVE 11.5 (2023-12-03) is the latest stable release; 12.0 has no stable release yet.
- The patterns, the check commands and the behaviour in Gotchas (filters, `require`
  spellings, seeding, push/pop errors across frames, save directory, error hook,
  `colorFromBytes`, key repeat) were run with the official LÖVE 11.5 x86_64 AppImage under
  Xvfb. Taken from the wiki only: `t.window.vsync` is a number since 11.0 and
  `love.math.colorFromBytes` arrived in 11.3.
- Sources: [LÖVE releases](https://github.com/love2d/love/releases),
  [love2d.org](https://love2d.org/), [11.5 `love.run`
  source](https://github.com/love2d/love/blob/11.5/src/modules/love/callbacks.lua),
  [love.filesystem](https://love2d.org/wiki/love.filesystem),
  [love.graphics.setDefaultFilter](https://love2d.org/wiki/love.graphics.setDefaultFilter),
  [Config Files](https://love2d.org/wiki/Config_Files).

skills.body:
---
name: pygame-core
description: >
  Builds and debugs 2D games in Python with pygame-ce (imported as pygame): the event-update-draw
  loop, delta time, Surfaces and Rects, Sprite groups and headless tests. Use when code imports
  pygame, or a window says not responding, speed differs per PC or pygame and pygame-ce conflict.
  Not for engine-neutral input or saves (`input-systems`, `save-systems`) or jump feel
  (`platformer`).
---

# pygame Core

Build and debug a pygame game. New code targets **pygame-ce 2.5.8**, the maintained
community fork; it installs as `pygame-ce` and imports as `pygame`. Legacy `pygame` 2.6
code mostly runs unchanged; pygame-ce-only APIs such as `FRect` and `get_frect()` need the
fork, which `getattr(pygame, "IS_CE", False)` detects.

## When to use

- Starting a pygame game, or fixing its loop, speed, input, drawing, sprite groups,
  collision, audio or text.
- Any project with `import pygame`, whichever package provides it.

**When not to use:** Python questions unrelated to pygame; 3D; portable design work owned by
the related skills below.

## Workflow

1. **Check the install.** `python -c "import pygame; print(pygame.version.ver,
   getattr(pygame, 'IS_CE', False))"`. Keep the project's package; for a new project use
   `pip install pygame-ce`.
2. **Keep logic testable.** Put rules in classes or functions that take `dt` and an input
   snapshot, so a test can drive them without a window. Only the loop touches the display.
3. **One loop per frame:** drain events, update with a clamped `dt`, draw, `flip()`. Use
   pixels per second, and float positions (`FRect` or `Vector2`).
4. **Load assets after `set_mode`**, then `convert()` / `convert_alpha()` once each.
5. **Verify headless.** Run the tests and a short scripted run with the dummy drivers (see
   the check below), then open the saved PNG. Report what ran. Feel, audio and real input
   still need a person: ask the user to play for a minute and report speed, controls and
   sound.

## Pattern: a loop that can run headless

```python
import argparse
import pygame

def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--frames", type=int, default=0, help="quit after N frames (0 = run)")
    ap.add_argument("--shot", help="save the last frame to this PNG")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    pygame.init()
    screen = pygame.display.set_mode((320, 180), pygame.SCALED)  # before any convert()
    clock = pygame.time.Clock()
    sprites = pygame.sprite.Group(Player((160, 90)))

    frame, running = 0, True
    while running:
        dt = min(clock.tick(60) / 1000, 0.05)          # clamp stalls (window drag, debugger)
        for event in pygame.event.get():
            if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
                running = False
        sprites.update(dt, pygame.key.get_pressed())
        screen.fill((18, 18, 28))
        sprites.draw(screen)
        pygame.display.flip()
        frame += 1
        if args.frames and frame >= args.frames:
            if args.shot:
                pygame.image.save(screen, args.shot)
            running = False
    pygame.quit()
```

```python
class Player(pygame.sprite.Sprite):
    def __init__(self, pos):
        super().__init__()
        self.image = pygame.image.load("player.png").convert_alpha()
        self.rect = self.image.get_frect(center=pos)   # FRect keeps sub-pixel positions
        self.speed = 120                               # pixels per second

    def update(self, dt, keys):
        move = pygame.Vector2(keys[pygame.K_RIGHT] - keys[pygame.K_LEFT],
                              keys[pygame.K_DOWN] - keys[pygame.K_UP])
        if move.length_squared():                      # zero vectors cannot be scaled
            move.scale_to_length(self.speed * dt)      # same speed on diagonals
```

  collision, audio or text.

   snapshot, so a test can drive them without a window. Only the loop touches the display.

5. **Verify headless.** Run the tests and a short scripted run with the dummy drivers (see

```python
    ap.add_argument("--shot", help="save the last frame to this PNG")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    pygame.init()
    screen = pygame.display.set_mode((320, 180), pygame.SCALED)  # before any convert()
    clock = pygame.time.Clock()
    sprites = pygame.sprite.Group(Player((160, 90)))

                running = False

        frame += 1
        if args.frames and frame >= args.frames:
            if args.shot:

            running = False
```

---
name: roblox-characters
description: >
  Roblox player characters: CharacterAdded lifecycle, Humanoid and HumanoidRootPart, R6, R15 and
  custom rigs, respawn and Tools. Use when a character script breaks after respawn, animations do
  not play or replicate, or sprint code fights the Humanoid. Not for hit validation
  (`roblox-networking`), forces and raycasts (`roblox-physics`) or cameras (`camera-systems`).
---

# Roblox characters

A `Player` is the durable identity; each `Character` is a replaceable session with its own
references, connections, animation tracks, and cleanup. Most character bugs are one character's
state leaking into the next.

## Workflow

1. **Read the character contract.** Avatar Settings (rig type, movement system), `StarterCharacter`,
   `StarterCharacterScripts`, `Players.CharacterAutoLoads`, `Workspace.PlayerCharacterDestroyBehavior`,
   the existing Animate or controller scripts, tools, tags, and collision groups. Extend what is
   there; do not add a second controller.
2. **Separate scopes.** Player-scope state survives respawn; character-scope state does not. Put
   each character's connections, tracks, and temporary instances in one cleanup scope.
3. **Bind existing and future characters.** Connect `CharacterAdded`, then bind `player.Character`
   if it already exists. On the server, do this for players already in `Players:GetPlayers()`.
4. **Resolve parts defensively.** `WaitForChild` with a timeout for `Humanoid`, the root part, and
   `Animator`; after every yield, check the character is still the current one before acting.
5. **Choose one movement owner per state.** Standard avatars use Humanoid movement or the
   Character Controller Library. Physical mechanics (dash, knockback, grapple) use an impulse or a
   constraint for their duration and hand control back cleanly.
6. **Own animation lifecycle.** Load through the rig's `Animator`, keep tracks and marker
   connections in the character scope, and stop them on cleanup. Markers drive presentation; any
   gameplay effect they trigger is validated on the server.
7. **Run the lifecycle check.** With the Studio MCP server connected, start play, respawn the
   player several times from `execute_luau` on the `Server` datamodel
   (`for _ = 1, 5 do player:LoadCharacterAsync() task.wait(1) end`), then read
   `get_console_output`: expect no errors and exactly one setup log per spawn. Without MCP, ask the
   user to reset five times in Test and once with two players in Server & Clients, and to report
   duplicated logs, stuck animations, or errors.

## Pattern: replaceable character scope

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local generation = 0
local connections: {RBXScriptConnection} = {}
local currentCharacter: Model? = nil

local function clearCharacter()
    generation += 1
    for _, connection in connections do connection:Disconnect() end
    table.clear(connections)
    currentCharacter = nil
end

local function bindCharacter(character: Model)
    -- Guard before teardown: a stale call must not clear a binding that is already current.
    if player.Character ~= character or currentCharacter == character then return end
    clearCharacter()
    currentCharacter = character
    local thisGeneration = generation
    local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid", 10)
    local root = character:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart", 10)
    -- A respawn during WaitForChild bumps generation and makes this call stale.
    if not humanoid or not root or generation ~= thisGeneration then return end

    table.insert(connections, humanoid.Died:Connect(function()
        if generation ~= thisGeneration then return end
        setCharacterUiEnabled(false)
    end))
    attachCurrentCharacterSystems(character, humanoid, root)
end

player.CharacterRemoving:Connect(function(character)
    if currentCharacter == character then clearCharacter() end
end)
player.CharacterAdded:Connect(bindCharacter)
if player.Character then task.defer(bindCharacter, player.Character) end
```

Use the project's cleanup utility when one exists rather than introducing a framework for three
connections. Server systems repeat this binding per `Player` and clear player-scope tables on
`PlayerRemoving`.

## Pattern: animation through Animator and markers

```lua
local animation = Instance.new("Animation")
animation.AnimationId = "rbxassetid://1234567890"
local track = animator:LoadAnimation(animation)
local markerConnection = track:GetMarkerReachedSignal("Commit"):Connect(function(parameter)
    playLocalSwingEffect(parameter) -- presentation only; the server validates any hit
end)

track:Play(0.1)
-- On character teardown:
markerConnection:Disconnect()
track:Stop(0.1)
animation:Destroy()
```

Rigs without a `Humanoid` need an `AnimationController` with an `Animator`. `Humanoid:LoadAnimation()`
is deprecated; always load through the `Animator`.

## Movement and rig rules

- If R6 is supported, do not hardcode R15 limb names. Prefer attachments, tags, or a small rig
  adapter; branch on `Humanoid.RigType` only where topology really differs.
- `HumanoidRootPart` is the usual assembly root, not a guarantee for custom models. Write down the
  custom rig contract and validate it at spawn.
- Setting `AssemblyLinearVelocity` is an instant change; use `ApplyImpulse` for one-off pushes and
  a `LinearVelocity` constraint for sustained control (details in `roblox-physics`).
- For new actions such as sprint or rebinding jump, use the Input Action System (`InputContext`,
  `InputAction`, `InputBinding`) instead of raw `UserInputService` hooks. Give your context a higher
  `Priority` (and `Sink`) than the default player contexts so it wins.
- If the place uses the Character Controller Library (Avatar Settings → Movement → Abilities) or a
  `ControllerManager`, extend its abilities and controllers. Layering `HumanoidStateType` changes
  on top of it fights the library.
- Tools move between `Backpack` and the character on equip. Listen to ancestry and the tool's
  `Equipped`/`Unequipped` events instead of assuming one parent.
- Change appearance with `Humanoid:ApplyDescriptionAsync()` and keep the applied
  `HumanoidDescription` up to date.
- Under Server Authority (`Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server`), gameplay animation runs inside
  bound simulation functions and the client may replace tracks during rollback, so look tracks up
  each frame with `Animator:GetTrackByAnimationId()` instead of caching them. Tools are not fully
  supported there yet; see `roblox-networking`.

## Gotchas

| Symptom | Likely cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|
| works once, breaks after reset | cached character, Humanoid or root | rebuild per `CharacterAdded`; clear on removal |
| callbacks fire twice after deaths | old character connections survived | character-scoped cleanup plus generation checks |
| memory grows with every respawn | old characters are only unparented, and tables still reference them | clear Instance-keyed tables; check `PlayerCharacterDestroyBehavior` |
| delayed setup edits the wrong rig | async work outlived its spawn | compare current character or generation after every yield |
| animation plays only locally or not at all | wrong Animator, side, or asset permission | inspect the rig's Animator, who loads it, and the asset owner |
| hit marker awards impossible hits | marker trusted as authority | marker for timing; server validates combat state |
| R6 or custom rig errors | R15 names assumed | rig contract and adapter; test every supported rig |
| tool disappears from a system | fixed Backpack or Character parent assumed | handle equip, unequip, and character replacement |
| custom force fights the Humanoid | two controllers own motion | one movement owner per state; restore on exit |

## Resources

- Read `references/lifecycle-and-animation.md` when a system spans respawns, supports several
  rigs, or owns animation and tool resources: server binding, death vs removal, custom-character
  checklist, and the lifecycle stress matrix.

## Related skills

- `roblox-physics`: forces, constraints, assemblies, and network ownership.
- `roblox-networking`: validating character actions and rejecting stale requests.
- `input-systems`: action mapping and responsive movement intent.
- `camera-systems`: cameras that follow a replaceable character.

## Version notes

Last verified: 2026-11-11.

- `Player:LoadCharacter()`, `Humanoid:ApplyDescription()` and `Humanoid:PlayEmote()` are deprecated
  in favour of `LoadCharacterAsync()`, `ApplyDescriptionAsync()` and `PlayEmoteAsync()`.
- The Character Controller Library was announced as released for live experiences in April 2026;
  its docs page still carried a beta note on the verification date. Avatar Settings needs a saved
  or published place.
- `Workspace.PlayerCharacterDestroyBehavior`, when enabled, destroys the old character on respawn
  and the `Player` object on leave.
- To re-check an API: append `.md` to its Creator Hub URL, or start from
  `https://create.roblox.com/docs/llms.txt`.

Sources: `https://create.roblox.com/docs/characters`,
`https://create.roblox.com/docs/animation/using`,
`https://create.roblox.com/docs/characters/character-controller-library`,
`https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Player`,
`https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Humanoid`,
`https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Workspace`,
`https://create.roblox.com/docs/projects/server-authority`,
`https://devforum.roblox.com/t/full-release-the-future-of-character-movement-character-controller-library/4565267`.
